answer: Randomized Identity Seals** Each agent must periodically refresh their identity by computing a verifiable random seal (e.g., VRF output) tied to a public nadir event—a global randomness beacon. The seal expires after a fixed horizon, forcing re-computation. Attackers cannot precompute future seals, as each requires solving a unique ivory-puzzle: a one-time PoW derived from the latest beacon. Per-identity cost scales with puzzle difficulty, requiring fresh compute per Sybil. Expired seals invalidate voting power or rewards.
